name: Italian
climateSuitability: Best for warm/hot zones (7-10). Good for all regions as first-year bees.
notes: Prone to robbing. Low propolis. High heat tolerance. Most forgiving for beginners.

name: Carniolan
climateSuitability: Best for cold zones (3-7). Excellent in Northeast, Upper Midwest, Pacific Northwest.
notes: Rapid spring buildup. Excellent cold hardiness. Poor heat tolerance. Low propolis.

name: Russian
climateSuitability: Best for extreme cold zones (3-5). Good for Mountain West and Great Plains.
notes: VSH trait for mite resistance. Slow spring buildup. Need 80-100 lbs stores for winter.

name: Buckfast
climateSuitability: Versatile across zones 4-9. Good for Northeast, Mountain West, Southeast.
notes: Tracheal mite resistant. Moderate to fast spring buildup. Good cold and heat tolerance.

name: Saskatraz
climateSuitability: Wide range zones 3-10. Best for Upper Midwest, Southeast, Southwest.
notes: Excellent varroa and tracheal mite resistance. Very high propolis. Good all-climate bee.

name: Caucasian
climateSuitability: Best for moderate zones (5-7) with lower mite pressure.
notes: Very high propolis which can be challenging. Slow spring buildup. Fair heat tolerance.

name: German Dark
climateSuitability: Best for cold zones (3-5) where temperament is less concern.
notes: Excellent cold hardiness. Poor heat tolerance. Not typically recommended due to aggression.

name: Africanized
climateSuitability: Only suitable for hot zones (9-11). NOT recommended for residential areas.
notes: WARNING: Extremely defensive. Requires experienced beekeepers only. High honey production. Excellent disease resistance. Illegal in some jurisdictions.

name: VSH Italian
climateSuitability: Wide range zones 4-10. Best for beekeepers dealing with varroa mites.
notes: Varroa Sensitive Hygiene trait bred into Italian stock. Best of both worlds: gentle temperament with strong mite resistance. Slightly lower honey production than standard Italian.
